lines: Drum pattern generator, a port of Mutable Instruments Grids: three trigger channels whose rhythms are read out of a map of ready-made patterns
Restarts the pattern at its first step and restarts the internal clock
Starts and stops the sequence, one press each way, or runs it only while held when the menu is set to momentary
Sets the internal tempo from 40 to 240 BPM; fully counter-clockwise the readout says Ext. and the sequence steps from the CLOCK input instead
Moves the reading point across the map of patterns from side to side, mixing the four patterns at its corners; in Euclidean mode it sets the length of channel 1 from 1 to 32 steps
Moves the reading point up and down the map of patterns, mixing the four patterns at its corners; in Euclidean mode it sets the length of channel 2 from 1 to 32 steps
Adds random variation to the pattern, redrawn at the start of every 32-step cycle; in Euclidean mode it sets the length of channel 3 from 1 to 32 steps
Sets how full the channel 1 pattern is, from silence to every step of it; in Euclidean mode it sets how many pulses are spread over that channel's length
Sets how full the channel 2 pattern is, from silence to every step of it; in Euclidean mode it sets how many pulses are spread over that channel's length
Sets how full the channel 3 pattern is, from silence to every step of it; in Euclidean mode it sets how many pulses are spread over that channel's length
Makes alternate steps uneven, lengthening the first half of each beat and shortening the second; the internal clock alone is swung, never an external one
Steps the sequence on each rising edge while the tempo knob is fully counter-clockwise, and patching a cable here drives that knob there; 4, 8 or 24 pulses make a quarter note
A rising edge restarts the pattern at its first step
Adds to the horizontal position on the map of patterns, 10V covering the full width
Adds to the vertical position on the map of patterns, 10V covering the full height
Adds to the amount of random variation, 10V covering the full range
Adds to the fullness of the channel 1 pattern, 10V covering the full range
Adds to the fullness of the channel 2 pattern, 10V covering the full range
Adds to the fullness of the channel 3 pattern, 10V covering the full range
Adds to the swing amount, 10V covering the full range
A rising edge starts or stops the sequence; in momentary run mode the sequence runs for as long as this is high
Fires on every step of channel 1, a 10V pulse of 1ms or a gate lasting the whole step when the menu is set to Gate
Fires on every step of channel 2, a 10V pulse of 1ms or a gate lasting the whole step when the menu is set to Gate
Fires on every step of channel 3, a 10V pulse of 1ms or a gate lasting the whole step when the menu is set to Gate
Fires on the accented steps of channel 1, or on any accented step of any channel when the menu is set to Accent / Clock / Reset
Fires on the accented steps of channel 2, or once on every step as a clock when the menu is set to Accent / Clock / Reset
Fires on the accented steps of channel 3, or once at the start of each pattern as a reset when the menu is set to Accent / Clock / Reset
Note — the sequence is stopped when the module is placed, so nothing comes out of the trigger outputs until the run button is pressed or a voltage is sent to the run input
Menu — Sequencer Mode — a heading over three items: Henri and Original each choose a built-in set of patterns, and Euclidean builds the patterns from a length and a fullness instead
Menu — Trigger Output Mode — a heading over 1ms Pulse and Gate, setting whether a trigger output sends a 1ms pulse or a gate lasting the whole step
Menu — Accent Output Mode — a heading over Individual accents and Accent / Clock / Reset, the second of which turns the three accent outputs into a common accent, a clock and a reset
Menu — Ext. Clock Resolution — a heading over 4 PPQN, 8 PPQN and 24 PPQN, setting how many pulses at the clock input make a quarter note
Menu — Run Mode — a heading over Toggle and Momentary, setting whether the run button latches or runs the sequence only while it is held
Menu — Randomise Tempo Knob — under the Randomisation heading, lets the tempo knob move when the patch is randomised; it is left alone otherwise

Sets how full the channel 3 pattern is, from silence to every step of it; in Euclidean mode it sets how many pulses are spread over that channel's length

Adds to the vertical position on the map of patterns, 10V covering the full height

Adds to the swing amount, 10V covering the full range
A rising edge starts or stops the sequence; in momentary run mode the sequence runs for as long as this is high
Fires on every step of channel 1, a 10V pulse of 1ms or a gate lasting the whole step when the menu is set to Gate
Fires on every step of channel 2, a 10V pulse of 1ms or a gate lasting the whole step when the menu is set to Gate
Fires on every step of channel 3, a 10V pulse of 1ms or a gate lasting the whole step when the menu is set to Gate
Fires on the accented steps of channel 1, or on any accented step of any channel when the menu is set to Accent / Clock / Reset
Fires on the accented steps of channel 2, or once on every step as a clock when the menu is set to Accent / Clock / Reset

Note — the sequence is stopped when the module is placed, so nothing comes out of the trigger outputs until the run button is pressed or a voltage is sent to the run input
Note — the pattern set and the external clock resolution are chosen from the two boxes on the panel rather than from the right-click menu
Menu — Trigger Output Mode — a heading over 1ms Pulse and Gate, setting whether a trigger output sends a 1ms pulse or a gate lasting the whole step
Menu — Accent Output Mode — a heading over Individual accents and Accent / Clock / Reset, the second of which turns the three accent outputs into a common accent, a clock and a reset
Menu — Run Mode — a heading over Toggle and Momentary, setting whether the run button latches or runs the sequence only while it is held
Menu — Randomise Tempo Knob — under the Randomisation heading, lets the tempo knob move when the patch is randomised; it is left alone otherwise
Stereo state-variable filter with a drive stage, a spread between the two channels' cutoffs and ten CV inputs
Sets the cutoff of both channels, an octave per unit of travel, from 13.75Hz at the bottom to 14080Hz at the top
Sets the resonance of both channels, from none at the bottom to a sharp peak at the top
Spreads the two cutoffs apart, moving the right channel up to an octave up or down
Sets how much of that spread is applied to the left channel in the opposite direction: at the bottom only the right channel moves, at the top the left moves as far the other way
Switches both channels between two poles and four, a 12dB or 24dB per octave slope
Switches both channels between low pass and band pass
Sets the gain into the filter, from 0.75 fully counter-clockwise to 10 fully clockwise, which overdrives its saturating stages
Attenuates and inverts a cutoff CV; at full clockwise a volt of that CV moves the cutoff by an octave
Attenuates and inverts a resonance CV; at full clockwise 10V covers the whole resonance range
Attenuates and inverts a drive CV; at full clockwise 10V covers the whole drive range
Attenuates and inverts a spacing CV; at full clockwise 10V covers the whole spread
Nothing in the module reads this knob; the spacing target is set by the Trgt slider alone
The left channel into the filter; with nothing patched to the right input this one feeds both channels
The right channel into the filter; with nothing patched to the left input this one feeds both channels
Adds to the cutoff of both channels at a volt per octave, through its own attenuverter
Adds to the resonance of both channels through its own attenuverter, 10V covering the full range
Adds to the input drive through its own attenuverter, 10V covering the full range
Adds to the spread between the two cutoffs through its own attenuverter, 10V covering the full range
Nothing in the module reads this jack; the spacing target is set by the Trgt slider alone
The filtered left channel
The filtered right channel
The two filtered channels summed and halved, for use in mono
Note — the two Trgt CV jacks and the attenuverters beside them are read nowhere in this version of the module, so the spacing target comes from its slider alone
Feline.notes: The Trgt CV jacks and their two attenuverters (params 11 and 16, inputs 6 and 11) are never read in Feline::step in 2.4.5; the spacing target comes from the slider alone.

lines: Stereo signal masher: two stereo inputs are driven into one of seventeen combination modes, with logic and pulse outputs taken from the result
Drives the X input into a saturating shaper, from silence at the bottom to four times gain at the top
Drives the Y input into a saturating shaper, from silence at the bottom to four times gain at the top
Sets the first parameter of the chosen combination mode; what it does changes with the mode, from a ring modulator's quadrant to a bit crusher's depth, and the display names it
Sets the second parameter of the chosen combination mode; what it does changes with the mode, from pulse width to a comparison threshold, and the display names it
Chooses the combination mode from seventeen: three ring modulators, a diode ring modulator, minimum and maximum, sign work, crossfade, flip-flop, PWM, and bitwise and floating-point mangling
Attenuates and inverts a type CV; 10V at full depth sweeps the whole list of modes
Attenuates and inverts the X gain CV; 10V at full depth covers the whole gain range
Attenuates and inverts the Y gain CV; 10V at full depth covers the whole gain range
Attenuates and inverts a Param A CV; 10V at full depth covers the whole range of that parameter
Attenuates and inverts a Param B CV; 10V at full depth covers the whole range of that parameter
Lets DC through to every output; with it off a 1Hz high-pass filter removes the offset the combination modes produce
The left channel of the X input; with nothing in the right X input this one feeds both
The right channel of the X input; with nothing in the left X input this one feeds both
The left channel of the Y input; with nothing in the right Y input this one feeds both
The right channel of the Y input; with nothing in the left Y input this one feeds both
Adds to the X gain through its own attenuverter
Adds to the Y gain through its own attenuverter
Moves through the list of combination modes, added to the Type knob through its own attenuverter
Adds to Param A through its own attenuverter
Adds to Param B through its own attenuverter
5V while the driven left X and left Y signals are both above 0V
5V while exactly one of the driven left X and left Y signals is above 0V
5V while the driven right X and right Y signals are both above 0V, despite the tooltip naming the left channel
5V while exactly one of the driven right X and right Y signals is above 0V, despite the tooltip naming the left channel
The left channel of the combined signal, saturated and reaching about 5V
The right channel of the combined signal, saturated and reaching about 5V
5V while both channels of the combined signal are above 0V
5V while exactly one channel of the combined signal is above 0V
A 5V pulse wave taken from the left combined signal, high while that signal lies between zero and half of full scale
A 5V pulse wave taken from the right combined signal, high while that signal lies between zero and half of full scale
A 5V pulse wave taken from the left combined signal, high in the lowest quarter and the upper half of its positive range, so it pulses twice as often as the single pulse output
A 5V pulse wave taken from the right combined signal, high in the lowest quarter and the upper half of its positive range, so it pulses twice as often as the single pulse output
Note — the two combined outputs take the internal channels the other way round from the logic and pulse outputs, so what is fed into the left X and Y inputs leaves by the right combined output
Amalgam.notes: Input 6 (MODE_CV_INPUT) is declared in the code with no widget on the panel and cannot be clicked. The tooltips on outputs 2 and 3 read 'X left AND Y left' and 'X left XOR Y left', but the code feeds them the right-hand channel. The Z left and Z right outputs are taken from the vector lanes the other way round from the pulse and logic outputs, so the channel fed by the left input arrives at Z right.

lines: Plate reverb after the Dattorro 1997 algorithm, able to run from a huge hall down to a short, tuneable resonant box
Sets how much of the input reaches the outputs unchanged
Sets the level of the reverb at the outputs
Delays the signal entering the plate by up to 500ms, leaving the dry path alone
Sets the high-pass filter on the signal entering the plate, 440Hz fully counter-clockwise falling to 13.75Hz fully clockwise, the reverse of the way the tooltip reads it
Sets the low-pass filter on the signal entering the plate, 440Hz fully counter-clockwise rising to 14080Hz fully clockwise
Scales every delay time inside the plate, from a small bright box to a large hall; in Tuned Mode the same travel covers five octaves of much shorter times
Sets how strongly the all-pass stages inside the plate smear the sound, from separate repeating echoes to a smooth wash
Sets the feedback inside the plate, from a short tail fully counter-clockwise to one that runs for minutes fully clockwise
Sets the low-pass filter inside the plate, 440Hz fully counter-clockwise rising to 14080Hz fully clockwise, which damps the top of the tail
Sets the high-pass filter inside the plate, 440Hz fully counter-clockwise falling to 13.75Hz fully clockwise, which thins the bottom of the tail
Sets the speed of the four LFOs that move the plate's delay lines, from one to a hundred times their base rate
Moves the turning point of those LFOs, giving a falling ramp fully counter-clockwise, a triangle at noon and a rising ramp fully clockwise
Sets how far the LFOs move the plate's delay lines, up to 16 samples
Freezes the plate: the tail repeats without decaying and no new signal enters it, for as long as the button is held unless Tog. is lit
Fades the output down, empties the plate's delay lines and fades back in
Makes the Hold button latch, one press freezing the plate and the next releasing it, in place of freezing only while held
Attenuates and inverts the dry level CV; at full depth a volt of that CV covers the whole range of the knob
Attenuates and inverts the wet level CV; at full depth a volt of that CV covers the whole range of the knob
Attenuates and inverts the input low cut CV; at full depth 10V covers the whole range of the knob
Attenuates and inverts the input high cut CV; at full depth 10V covers the whole range of the knob
Attenuates and inverts the size CV; at full depth 10V covers the whole range of the knob
Attenuates and inverts the diffusion CV; at full depth 10V covers the whole range of the knob
Attenuates and inverts the decay CV; at full depth 10V takes the decay from its shortest to its longest
Attenuates and inverts the reverb high cut CV; at full depth 10V covers the whole range of the knob
Attenuates and inverts the reverb low cut CV; at full depth 10V covers the whole range of the knob
Attenuates and inverts the modulation rate CV; at full depth 10V covers the whole range of the knob
Attenuates and inverts the modulation shape CV; at full depth 10V covers the whole range of the knob
Attenuates and inverts the modulation depth CV; at full depth 10V covers the whole range of the knob
Puts the Size knob on an exponential law over much shorter delay times, so that a small plate can be tuned to a pitch
Passes the input through four all-pass stages before the plate; with it dark the input enters undiffused and early echoes stay distinct
The left input; with nothing patched to the right input this one feeds both channels
The right input; with nothing patched to the left input this one feeds both channels
Adds to the dry level through its own attenuverter
Adds to the wet level through its own attenuverter
Lengthens the pre-delay exponentially, 10V adding the full 500ms; the menu can halve that sensitivity
Adds to the input low cut through its own attenuverter
Adds to the input high cut through its own attenuverter
Adds to the plate size through its own attenuverter
Adds to the diffusion through its own attenuverter
Adds to the decay through its own attenuverter
Adds to the reverb high cut through its own attenuverter
Adds to the reverb low cut through its own attenuverter
Adds to the modulation rate through its own attenuverter
Adds to the modulation shape through its own attenuverter
Adds to the modulation depth through its own attenuverter
Above 0.5V the plate freezes; with Tog. lit each rising edge switches the freeze on or off instead
Above 0.5V the plate's delay lines are emptied, with a short fade out and back in
The left output, carrying the dry signal and the left side of the reverb
The right output, carrying the dry signal and the right side of the reverb
Menu — Predelay CV Sensitivity — a heading over Normal (1x) and Low (0.5x), the second of which halves the effect of the pre-delay CV input
Menu — Input Sensitivity — a heading over 0dB and -18dB, the second of which drops the level into the plate and keeps hot signals out of saturation
Menu — Output Saturation — a heading over Off and On, the second of which replaces the hard 10V clip at the outputs with a soft saturating stage
Plateau.notes: Param 16 (CLEAR_TOGGLE_PARAM) is declared with no widget. The four damping knobs are offset by 5 inside the code, so their tooltip readings in Hz do not match the filter frequencies actually set; the low cut knobs run backwards against their readings. The decay CV is rescaled such that even an unpatched decay input adds 0.1 to the decay knob.

lines: Virtual-analogue synth voice: one oscillator with a sub and noise, a mixer, a state-variable filter, an LFO and an ADSR envelope, polyphonic from the channel count at its V/Oct inputs
Shifts the oscillator in octaves, from 32 foot two octaves down to 2 foot two octaves up
Tunes the oscillator across an octave either way, in semitone steps on Semi and smoothly on Cont
Tunes the oscillator up or down by a semitone
Sets how far the chosen source moves the oscillator pitch, reaching an octave at the top with a squared response
Sets whether the envelope raises or lowers the oscillator pitch, for when the envelope is the pitch modulation source
Chooses whether the LFO or the envelope modulates the oscillator pitch
Sets the width of the pulse wave, a square fully counter-clockwise narrowing to nothing fully clockwise
Sets how far the chosen source moves the pulse width, reaching half the cycle at the top
Chooses what moves the pulse width: the envelope, the LFO, or the PWM input
Sets whether the envelope widens or narrows the pulse, for when the envelope is the pulse width source
Makes the coarse tuning of the oscillator step in whole semitones instead of running smoothly
Slews the pitch from the V/Oct inputs, from an instant jump at the bottom to a slow glide at the top
Sets the sub oscillator against the main one: two octaves down, one octave down, three quarters of its frequency, unison, one and a half times it, an octave up, or two octaves up
Chooses the sub oscillator's wave: a pulse at three-quarter width, a square, or a sawtooth
Chooses white or pink noise, both for the mixer's noise channel and for the noise output in the LFO section
Sets the level of the sawtooth wave in the mixer
Sets the level of the pulse wave in the mixer
Sets the level of the sub oscillator in the mixer
Sets the level of the noise in the mixer
Sets the level of the external input in the mixer
Sets the filter cutoff, an octave per unit of travel, from 13.75Hz at the bottom to 14080Hz at the top
Sets the filter resonance, from none at the bottom to a sharp peak at the top
Sets a high-pass filter on the signal leaving the filter, 13.75Hz at the bottom rising to 14080Hz at the top
Switches the filter between two poles and four, a 12dB or 24dB per octave slope
Sets how far the LFO moves the filter cutoff, reaching five octaves at the top with a squared response
Sets how much of the V/Oct pitch is added to the filter cutoff, from none at the bottom to an octave of cutoff per octave played at the top
Sets how far the envelope moves the filter cutoff, reaching ten octaves at the top
Sets whether the envelope opens or closes the filter
Attenuates and inverts a filter cutoff CV; fully clockwise that CV moves the cutoff an octave per volt
Sets the LFO frequency, 0.1Hz fully counter-clockwise and doubling every unit of travel to about 205Hz
Tunes the LFO up or down by half an octave
Smooths the LFO shape that drives the pitch, pulse width and filter modulation; the LFO output jacks stay unsmoothed
Chooses which LFO shape drives the pitch, pulse width and filter modulation: sine, triangle, rising saw, falling ramp, square, sample and hold, or noise
Sets the envelope's attack, from 1ms at the bottom to 10 seconds at the top, ten times longer with Long selected
Sets the envelope's decay, from 1ms at the bottom to 10 seconds at the top, ten times longer with Long selected
Sets the level the envelope holds while the gate stays high
Sets the envelope's release, from 1ms at the bottom to 10 seconds at the top, ten times longer with Long selected
Multiplies every envelope stage time by ten
Makes the envelope cycle through attack and decay over and over once it has been started
Raises the gate for as long as it is held, on the first polyphonic channel
Chooses what opens the VCA: the envelope, or the gate itself smoothed by a 90Hz slew
Attenuates and inverts the VCA level CV; fully clockwise 10V covers the whole range of the VCA
Sets the oscillator pitch at a volt per octave, added to the other V/Oct input; the channel count here sets the module's polyphony
Moves the pulse width while the PWM switch is set to Ext, 10V covering the full range
Opens the envelope while it is above 1V
A voltage above 1V restarts the envelope from its attack
An outside signal into the mixer, at the level set by the Ext fader
Adds to the filter cutoff through its own attenuverter, an octave per volt at full depth
Adds to the filter resonance, 10V covering the whole range
Every volt here doubles the LFO frequency
A rising edge takes a new value at the LFO's sample and hold output
A rising edge restarts the LFO at the beginning of its cycle
Adds to the VCA level through its own attenuverter
The oscillator's sawtooth wave, 5V peak
The oscillator's pulse wave, 5V peak, at the width set by the pulse width controls
The sub oscillator's wave, 5V peak
The five mixer channels summed, taken before the filter
The filter's output, after the high-pass stage and before the VCA
The voice output, the filtered signal through the VCA, clamped at 10V
The LFO's sine wave, 5V peak, running whatever the LFO wave switch is set to
The LFO's triangle wave, 5V peak, running whatever the LFO wave switch is set to
The LFO's rising sawtooth, 5V peak, running whatever the LFO wave switch is set to
The LFO's falling ramp, 5V peak, running whatever the LFO wave switch is set to
The LFO's square wave, 5V peak, running whatever the LFO wave switch is set to
A new random level at every rise of the LFO's square wave, 5V peak, and at every rise at the trigger input
White or pink noise at 5V peak, whichever the noise switch selects
The envelope, 0 to 10V
The envelope inverted, 0 down to -10V
Note — the VCA output rests at 0V until a gate arrives at the gate input or the manual gate button is on; the oscillator, mixer and filter outputs run without one
Interzone.notes: Input 9 (FILTER_INPUT) is declared in the code with no widget on the panel. The LFO slew knob only smooths the LFO value used for internal modulation; the seven LFO output jacks carry the unsmoothed shapes.

lines: Wavetable oscillator with a phase shaper, an output mangler, a low-pass gate, a sub oscillator and two FM channels, playing 64 built-in wavetables or eight banks of your own
Shifts the oscillator by up to three octaves either way
Tunes the oscillator across an octave either way
Tunes the oscillator up or down by half a semitone
Attenuates and inverts a V/Oct input; fully clockwise that input moves the pitch an octave per volt
Chooses the wavetable, one of 64 built in, or one of the eight user banks while User is lit
Scans through the waves of the chosen table, crossfading between neighbouring waves
Attenuates and inverts a bank CV; 10V at full depth steps through every bank
Attenuates and inverts a wave CV; 10V at full depth scans the whole table
Chooses one of 27 ways to bend the phase that reads the wavetable, from Bend and Tilt through mirroring, stepping, buzzing and rising or falling sine shapes
Sets how far the phase shaper bends the wave, leaving it untouched fully counter-clockwise
Attenuates and inverts a shaper type CV; 10V at full depth runs through every shaper type
Attenuates and inverts a shaper depth CV; 10V at full depth covers the whole depth range
Chooses one of eleven ways to mangle the oscillator's output: bit crushing, quantising, three bitwise operations, overdrive, ring modulation, sharpening, sine shaping, folding or mirroring
Sets how strongly the enhancer mangles the output, leaving it untouched fully counter-clockwise
Attenuates and inverts an enhancer type CV; 10V at full depth runs through every enhancer type
Attenuates and inverts an enhancer depth CV; 10V at full depth covers the whole depth range
Sets how quickly the low-pass gate opens when it is triggered
Sets how quickly the low-pass gate closes once it has opened
Attenuates and inverts an attack CV; 10V at full depth covers the whole attack range
Attenuates and inverts a decay CV; 10V at full depth covers the whole decay range
Feeds the oscillator's output back into its own phase, bending the wave into harder shapes; with a cable in the skew input this knob attenuates that CV instead and the fixed amount drops to zero
Sets how much sub oscillator is mixed into the main output; the sub output jack carries it at full level whatever this is set to
Crossfades the sub oscillator's shape from sine through sawtooth and square to a square that flips on each cycle of the main wave
Steps the low-pass gate through VCA, filter and both, lit red, green and blue in turn; held for half a second it takes the gate out of the signal path and puts it back
Lengthens the range of the low-pass gate's attack and decay
Makes the voltage at the low-pass gate's trigger inputs set how far it opens, in place of treating anything positive as fully open
Makes the low-pass gate run as a one-shot, so its attack and decay play out whatever the length of the trigger
Attenuates the CV at its own FM VCA input, which sets the depth of that FM channel; with nothing patched there that channel stays wide open
Sets how much of its own FM input reaches the oscillator
Restricts its own sync input to the first quarter of the oscillator's cycle, which softens the sync
Plays from the eight user wavetable banks in place of the 64 built-in ones
Switches the FM channels from phase modulation to true frequency modulation, at 1000Hz per unit of the summed FM signal
Puts the low-pass gate before the enhancer rather than after it
Applies the phase shaper after the FM has been added to the phase rather than before it
Divides the oscillator frequency by 100 and lets the main and raw outputs pass DC, which turns the module into an LFO
Holds the oscillator frequency at zero and resets its phase, leaving FM, skew and sync the only things that move it
Makes the displays show each value with its CV added, rather than the knob position alone
Sets the pitch at a volt per octave through its own attenuverter
Moves through the wavetable banks through its own attenuverter, 10V at full depth covering all of them
Scans through the waves of the table through its own attenuverter, 10V at full depth covering the whole table
Moves through the shaper types through its own attenuverter
Adds to the shaper depth through its own attenuverter
Moves through the enhancer types through its own attenuverter
Adds to the enhancer depth through its own attenuverter
Sets the depth of its own FM channel through its own attenuator; with nothing patched here that channel is wide open
An FM signal into the oscillator at the level set by its own knob, as phase modulation or, with True lit, as frequency modulation
A rising edge resets the oscillator's phase in the manner set by the sync mode display
Adds to the low-pass gate's attack through its own attenuverter
Adds to the low-pass gate's decay through its own attenuverter
Opens the low-pass gate; with Velo lit the voltage here sets how far it opens, a tenth of the voltage being full
Bends the wave by feeding the oscillator's output back into its phase, by the amount the Skew knob sets for this jack
The oscillator's own ramp, rising from -5V to 5V over each cycle
A 5V pulse each time the oscillator's phase wraps round
The phase after the shaper has bent it, a ramp between -5V and 5V
The wavetable's output before the enhancer and the low-pass gate, 5V peak and DC blocked
The enhancer's own output, 5V peak and DC blocked
The low-pass gate's envelope, 0 to 10V
The sub oscillator an octave below the main one, 5V peak
The voice output: wavetable, enhancer, sub oscillator and low-pass gate together, 5V peak, or 12dB quieter when the menu says so
Note — the eight user banks are empty when the module is placed and hold silence, so loading WAV files through the User Bank Manager comes before switching the oscillator over to user waves
Note — the three name displays open the lists of wavetable banks, shaper types and enhancer types, so a table or a type can be picked by name rather than by turning its knob
Note — the sync mode display chooses what a sync pulse does: hard sync, a fifth, an octave up or down, rise, fall, pull, push, hold, one shot, lock shot or reverse
Menu — Open — under the User Bank Manager heading, replaces the panel with the wavetable editor, where WAV files are read into the eight user banks, renamed, cloned and exported
Menu — Number of voices — under the Voicing heading, sets the polyphony, from automatic to a fixed count up to sixteen
Menu — Reduce level by 12dB — under the Output level heading, drops the main output from 5V peak to about 1.25V
Menu — Red LED — under the Display style heading, colours the panel's readouts; Yellow LED, Green LED, Blue LED and White LED are the other choices
Terrorform.notes: The sync mode, the wavetable bank, the shaper type and the enhancer type are also chosen from displays on the panel rather than from the right-click menu; only the bank, shaper and enhancer choices are parameters, so only those three can be clicked for help.

lines: Four-operator FM oscillator whose operators read wavetables and shape their own phase, playing a chord voice and a second independently tuned voice at the same time
Chooses the chord voice A plays, from a single note through intervals and triads up to eleventh chords, 39 in all
Turns the chord over, up to ten steps either way, lifting or dropping notes by an octave a time
Pulls the chord's notes out of tune with each other, spreading them by up to two and a half semitones in alternating directions
Makes an inversion move every note of the chord together, rather than lifting one note at a time
Shifts voice A by up to three octaves either way
Tunes voice A across an octave either way
Tunes voice A up or down by about half a semitone
Shifts voice B by up to three octaves either way
Tunes voice B across an octave either way
Tunes voice B up or down by about half a semitone
Chooses one of 23 algorithms, the pattern of which operators modulate which and which reach the output
Adds to the phase shaping of all four operators at once
Raises or lowers the level of every operator that modulates another in the chosen algorithm, which brightens or darkens the FM without moving the carriers
Feeds operator 4 back into itself, up to a quarter of full depth, which takes its wave towards noise
Attenuates and inverts the chord CV; at full depth 10V sweeps the whole list of chords
Attenuates and inverts the inversion CV; at full depth a volt moves the inversion by one step
Attenuates and inverts the detune CV; at full depth 10V covers the whole detune range
Attenuates and inverts the algorithm CV; at full depth 10V steps through all 23 algorithms
Attenuates and inverts the feedback CV; at full depth 10V covers the whole feedback range
Attenuates and inverts the brightness CV; at full depth 10V covers the whole brightness range
Attenuates and inverts the shape CV; at full depth 10V covers the whole shaping range
Divides every operator's frequency by 100, turning the four of them into LFOs
Resets the phase of all four operators for as long as it is held
Multiplies that operator's frequency, in 27 steps from an eighth of it up to 24 times it
Tunes that operator across an octave either way
Tunes that operator up or down by a quarter of an octave
Scans through the waves of that operator's wavetable, crossfading between neighbours
Bends the phase that reads that operator's wave, in the shaping mode chosen on its settings page
Sets that operator's output level, which for an operator that modulates another is the depth of that modulation
Opens and closes that operator's settings pages, which carry its wavetable, its shaping and sync modes and the destinations of its four assignable modulation inputs
Applies that operator's phase shaping after the modulation has been added to its phase rather than before
Divides that operator's frequency by 100
Restricts sync to the first quarter of that operator's cycle, which softens it
Switches on sync for that operator, from its modulator in the algorithm; sync is only processed while a cable is in one of that operator's four assignable modulation inputs
Takes that operator's own output jack from before its level knob, so the jack stays at full level however low the knob is
Shows the wave page of that operator's settings, where the wavetable and the shaping mode are chosen
Shows the first modulation page of that operator's settings, where the destinations of its assignable modulation inputs are chosen
Shows the second modulation page of that operator's settings, where the rest of its modulation routing and its sync mode are chosen
Attenuates and inverts one assignable modulation input for that operator, sending it to the destination picked on the operator's settings page
Attenuates and inverts a pitch CV for that operator; fully clockwise it moves the operator an octave per volt
Attenuates and inverts a wave scan CV for that operator; at full depth 10V scans the whole wavetable
Attenuates and inverts a phase shaping CV for that operator; at full depth 10V covers the whole shaping range
Attenuates and inverts a level CV for that operator; at full depth 10V covers the whole level range
Moves through the list of chords through its own attenuverter
Turns the chord over through its own attenuverter, a volt per inversion step at full depth
Adds to the chord detune through its own attenuverter
Moves through the algorithms through its own attenuverter
Adds to the operator 4 feedback through its own attenuverter
Adds to the brightness through its own attenuverter
Adds to the phase shaping of all four operators through its own attenuverter
Sets voice A's pitch at a volt per octave, the voice that plays the chord
Sets voice B's pitch at a volt per octave, the voice that plays alone
An assignable modulation input for that operator, reaching the destination chosen on its settings page through its own attenuverter; a cable in any of the four also lets that operator be synced
Moves that operator's pitch through its own attenuverter, an octave per volt at full depth
Scans through that operator's wavetable through its own attenuverter
Adds to that operator's phase shaping through its own attenuverter
Adds to that operator's level through its own attenuverter
The left side of voice A, with the chord's notes spread across the stereo pair; with nothing patched to the right output this one carries the whole chord in mono
The right side of voice A, with the chord's notes spread across the stereo pair
Operator 1 on its own, taken from voice A or voice B as the menu chooses, and from before the level knob while Pre is lit
Operator 2 on its own, taken from voice A or voice B as the menu chooses, and from before the level knob while Pre is lit
Operator 3 on its own, taken from voice A or voice B as the menu chooses, and from before the level knob while Pre is lit
Operator 4 on its own, taken from voice A or voice B as the menu chooses, and from before the level knob while Pre is lit
Voice B on its own, the voice tuned by its own octave, coarse and fine knobs
Chooses which of the 35 wavetables that operator reads, the same table serving voice A and voice B
Note — a chord of more than three notes is shared between two engines, and the individual operator outputs then carry only part of it
Menu — Operator Sync Source — a heading over Parent and Neighbour: Parent syncs each operator from whatever modulates it in the algorithm, Neighbour from the operator numbered above it
Menu — Operator Outputs Source — a heading over Voice A and Voice B, choosing which of the two voices reaches the four single-operator outputs
Dexter.notes: Params 20 and 21 (VOCT_1_DEPTH_PARAM, VOCT_2_DEPTH_PARAM) and each operator's misc menu button are declared with no widget. Each operator's wave bank knob sits at the same place as its multiplier knob, but the two are never visible together: DexterWidget::step hides the multiplier while the settings page is open and shows the bank knob only on the wave page, so a click reaches whichever one is on screen and both are tagged. The same holds for the three settings page buttons, which are shown only while the settings page is open, over the hidden wave, shape and level knobs. An operator's SYNC button has no effect until a cable is patched into one of that operator's four assignable modulation inputs, because DexterCore only processes sync while such a jack is connected.
